correctness.rationale: Both deletion-minimality and private-neighbor predicates agree for all 2^n vertex subsets of P_n for 1<=n<=11. Exact all-support VC and all-branch adaptive recurrences reproduce path dimensions, including 462 rejected five-supports on P11, a 32-leaf depth-five tree, and 36<64 preventing depth six. The original mathematical proofs of support-vertex gluing and product additivity establish the all-s connected-tree identities. 1296 joined two-module concept pairs were separately checked.

evidence: Rote, arXiv:1903.04517, Theorems 1.1 and 1.2, optimize numbers of minimal dominating sets and enumeration delay; these are not VC/Littlestone dimension bounds.
Petr-Portier-Versteegen, arXiv:2206.13182, Theorem 1.2, bounds the number of MINIMUM (size-optimal) dominating sets in forests, distinct from INCLUSION-MINIMAL dominating sets.
Earlier forest maximal-independent-set results concern an inclusion-proper subfamily of the present concepts.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A known maximal-independent-set gap does not transfer by monotonicity to a strictly larger concept class: both VC and Littlestone dimensions are monotone under class inclusion, but strict inequality of the dimensions is not. Counting bounds do not determine both ranks. No stronger general theorem that forces this P11 result was found in inspected primary work.

evidence: An inclusion-minimal dominating set is a minimal transversal of the closed-neighborhood hypergraph; the vertex-incidence set system here is the family of transversals itself, not the neighborhood hypergraph.
Rote 2019 arXiv:1903.04517 Section 2 (private-neighbor criterion), Section 4 (minimal-set enumeration), plus whole-document text checks of shattering and online-dimension terminology.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Translated the claim among inclusion-minimal domination, minimal hitting sets of closed neighborhoods, their incidence traces, and first-query adaptive rank. A generic result on transversal enumeration or on the VC dimension of the INPUT neighborhood hypergraph would not imply the finite (4,5) incidence-family dimensions. Neither matching formulation nor equivalent P11 values were located in these actual searches.

originality.rationale: No inspected primary theorem covers the first P11 (VC,Ldim)=(4,5) result or the resulting connected degree-four tree gap. Rote 2019 already supplies the private-neighbor/gluing principle, which is credited rather than asserted new. Earlier maximal-independent-set forest results and minimum-cardinality domination counts have different conclusion/assumptions; comparison is by implication, not wording. Priority uncertainty remains.
residual_risks: Older hypergraph-transversal or learning literature might encode the same minimal domination incidence dimensions under different names; no search establishes absolute priority.
Only relevant portions and full-text term checks of the primary PDFs were inspected; opaque terminology elsewhere is a residual risk.

value.rationale: The first path size where a natural inclusion-minimal domination concept class separates static from adaptive vertex shattering is a meaningful finite boundary. This finite obstruction, combined with a reusable leaf-support factorization, yields exactly VC 4s and Ldim 5s on connected degree-four trees, an unbounded gap with a sharp linear rate for the displayed family. The finite table is not an arbitrary isolated value.
